Dr Jack Thomas

Department of Gastroenterology

City Hospital

Main Road

Still water

Dear Dr Thomas,

Re: Mr Patrick Newton, aged 25 years

I am writing this letter to refer you Mr Newton, a 25-year-old accountant, whose features are suggestive of
inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Your diagnosis and assessment would be highly appreciated.

Regarding his social and medical history, he is a smoker and he has a six- month history of low-grade
intermittent joint pain and anxiety for which he has been managed accordingly. Moreover, he has a family
history of Crohn's disease.

Today, Mr Newton attended my surgery complaining of a 4 month history of mild diarrhea and low-grade
intermittent right lower quadrant abdominal pain associated with lethargy, anorexia and weight loss of 3
kg in the last 4 months. On examination, he was febrile. Although his abdomen showed generalised
tenderness, there were no hepato or splenomegaly. Furthermore, his FBE revealed increase in WBC.
However, a decrease in both RBC and hemoglobin. In addition, his CPR and ESR were both elevated and his
faecal occult blood test showed a positive result. Thus, he was consulted about his IBD and was advised on
smoking cessation.

In light of the above, I would be grateful if you could assess and manage his condition as you think
appropriate. If you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
